items.d: The trade deal is unlikely lower food prices for shoppers, but should boost the economy more than other post-Brexit agreements.

items.t: Could you spot a fake banknote?

items.t: The secret cyber scramble to protect UK fridge freezers
items.d: A behind the scenes cyber-security operation has taken place to secure tens of thousands of refrigeration units from hackers, the BBC has learned.

items.t: Bridgetown AI summit to tackle safety as risks outpace capacity to respond
items.d: UN Secretary-General António Guterres is heading to Barbados to co-host a special summit on artificial intelligence (AI) safety on Monday, aimed at closing the gap between accelerating risks and many countries’ capacity to deal with the pace of development.

items.t: ‘You will not be alone’: General Assembly President tells Rohingya refugees after genocide ruling
items.d: A day after the UN’s highest court found that Myanmar had committed genocide against the Rohingya, the President of the General Assembly visited the refugee camps in Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh, urging the world to turn the landmark judgement into action.

items.t: West Bank: Record settler attacks mar olive harvest as UN urges Israel to protect farmers
items.d: Israeli settlers have carried out more than 400 attacks causing casualties or property damage during this year’s olive harvest in the occupied West Bank – more than in any previous season, UN agencies and humanitarian NGOs said on Friday.

items.t: Shattered playgrounds and freezing classrooms: Inside Ukraine’s deadliest year for children
items.d: Amid the ruins of a twice-bombed Kyiv kindergarten as a day-long power cut continued, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) on Friday highlighted the dangers to youngsters enduring another brutal winter in Ukraine, as child casualty numbers rise to record levels.

items.t: WFP plans to assist 91 million in 2027 as hunger crisis deepens
items.d: The World Food Programme (WFP) will require $12.1 billion to assist 91 million people next year but warned that millions more will go hungry as funding shortfalls continue and another global food crisis looms.

items.t: COP31: Countries demand stronger climate deal amid deadlock in Antalya
items.d: A group of countries from Europe, Africa, Latin America and the Pacific has challenged the proposed COP31 agreement, demanding explicit action on fossil fuels and stronger climate finance. With the summit due to close on Friday, tensions are rising as activists warn the talks are headed for failure, and negotiators search for a deal that nearly 200 governments can accept.

items.t: Afghanistan restrictions prevent pregnant women from seeking medical help
items.d: Aid and development agencies in Afghanistan warned on Friday of an escalating “assault” on the rights and freedoms of women and girls that is preventing growing numbers from accessing vital medical care.

items.t: What are heat pumps and how much do they cost?
items.d: The government wants more homes to have heat pumps to cut fossil fuel use and drive down energy bills.
